SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.78
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows clear alkene signatures: strong =C–H stretches at 3022/3098 cm⁻¹ (supported by GFQ-003) and a C=C stretch at 1635 cm⁻¹, plus the characteristic terminal vinyl out-of-plane bands normally near ~990/910 cm⁻¹ appearing here at 957 and 893 cm⁻¹. A strong carbonyl near 1748 cm⁻¹ is consistent with a peroxide/ester-type C=O (higher than typical acids/amides). Very intense bands at 1299 and 1041 cm⁻¹ match ester C–O stretching components, and prominent bands in the 830–900 cm⁻¹ region (837, 893 cm⁻¹) support an O–O stretch from a peroxide. This unique combination of a terminal alkene and peroxy-ester functionalities best fits C=CCOC(=O)OOO (candidate 4); other candidates (amides, acids, aldehydes, N-oxides) would show different key features (e.g., amide/acid C=O near 1650–1725, aldehyde C–H at 2720–2820, or strong N→O around 1250 without peroxide O–O bands).
